_REVISION_2026-07-28: Round 2. The council's two [high] objections were (prior_art) that this entry restated the no-inert-control invariant in local terms three times while requires_invariant sat empty, and (checkability) that the 'no activation handler' third of the must_not had no check at all, deferred or otherwise. Both are answered structurally rather than by rewording: the invariant is now REFERENCED and the clauses it owns are deleted from this entry, and what remains in must_not is the one thing the invariant does NOT cover — a JS-bound activation handler on an element that is not a rendered button — which now carries its own check naming its own missing capability. Four silent gaps the council named (stay-hidden, degraded state, absence_semantics, the openable half of the split) now each have a check: two of them executable, two declared. See NOTES 2026-07-28e/f.
name: feed-driven-teaser-list
display_name: Teaser list rendered from a data feed, with an honest openable/inert split
description: A list whose rows are cloned from a hidden template and filled from a feed. Whether a row is a control is decided by the DATA, not by the template: a row whose record carries the linked content becomes a real link, and a row whose record does not is rendered so that it satisfies the no-inert-control invariant rather than being offered as openable.

contract.outcome: the row is a real control; what activation DOES is the referencing journey's clause, not this component's
contract.note: this component contract stops at 'is a control / is not a control'. The behaviour behind the control belongs to a micro-journey entry that requires this contract (here: teaser-detail-deeplink).
contract._outcome_note: REVISED 2026-07-29 (round 4, prior_art [medium]). This read 'carries a genuine href and remains keyboard-reachable' — the affirmative mirror of no-inert-control ('no placeholder href, no tab stop') restated in local prose. The two states were purged of exactly this two rounds ago and the contract was missed. Referenced now, not restated. The seat was right that a clause satisfying an invariant should say so rather than paraphrase it.

_SCHEMA_DELTA: states / data_contract / degraded_states are fields the draft DDL does not have — see HARVEST_01 §3.

states.condition: the row's feed record lacks the field the linked content lives in
states._must_not_note: REVISED 2026-07-28. This list used to read 'carry an href', 'carry a tabindex', 'carry an activation handler'. The first two ARE the no-inert-control invariant ('no placeholder href, no tab stop, no rendered button') restated in local terms, which is the drift the invariants table exists to end — they are now referenced via requires_invariant and enforces_invariant instead. What is left is the one thing the invariant does not reach: a click handler bound by JS to an element that is not a rendered button. That is genuinely local, genuinely the worst case (a row that LOOKS inert and is not), and it is the clause the council found uncovered.
states.outcome: the row shows its teaser text and is visibly not offered as openable
states.why: the template ships a placeholder href='#'. Cloning it for a row with nowhere to go MANUFACTURES a dead control — the invariant's defect class exactly (bugs_open/023; the 2026-07-22 gauntlet correction). Stripping it is not cosmetic: it is the contract.
states.evidence: archive_loader_new.js --static branch removes href AND tabindex; live check B.3; feed carries 7 openable + 1 inert, so the split is exercised by real data

states._must_note: REVISED 2026-07-28. 'have its own href removed before any clone is appended' was the second restatement of the invariant and is removed from this list; it is carried by requires_invariant and checked by template_row_not_a_control. 'stay hidden' stays because it is local and, as of today, it is the half of this clause a static check can actually assert — see template_row_stays_hidden.
states.why: the un-cloned template is itself markup on the page; left with href='#' and visible it would be a dead control. Hidden-ness is what makes the placeholder harmless BEFORE the loader runs, which is why it is asserted separately and at a tier that can see it.
states.evidence: archive_loader_new.js: tmpl.removeAttribute("href") before the clone loop; served markup carries `hidden` and `data-archive-template` (fetched 2026-07-28)

states.outcome: the empty-state line remains visible; it is hidden only after at least one row renders

data_contract.absence_semantics: a missing optional field hides its slot rather than rendering an orphan separator — vonc: the stat dot is hidden when the entry has no stat, because there are no invented participation numbers any more

degraded_states.outcome: the shell and the empty state are left exactly as built — no half-populated rows, no invented error UI
degraded_states.checked_by: degraded_state_leaves_the_shell_intact (declared unassertable — see its reason; it is no longer a silent gap)

checks.note: NEW 2026-07-28, answering the council's 'stay hidden has no check anywhere' — and it is executable TODAY, not deferred. A missing hidden attribute fails, which is the whole point: the template's placeholder href is harmless only because nothing can reach the element. This is the one half of the openable/inert split a static look at the page can honestly assert, because the template is the only one of the three row states that is actually served.

RE-TIERED TO 4 ON 2026-07-28, AND PUT BACK ON 2026-07-29 BECAUSE THE COUNCIL WAS RIGHT. The deferral_honesty seat: "Moving a failing check to a tier the platform doesn't execute, rather than reporting the failure, reads as evasion even with the honest note attached." That is the same suspicion I had already recorded about my own reasoning in WRONG_CALLS.md — that re-tiering was the reading which made my own red result disappear — and an independent seat reaching it from the other direction settles it. So this runs at Tier 2 and it FAILS: the served template carries href="#". Whether that is a real defect or is forgiven by the platform's data-runtime-fill exemption is bugs_open/137, and it is not this entry's job to pre-empt the answer by hiding the question. The consequence is accepted deliberately: while this fails, the vonc fork cannot reach 'verified'. An entry that cannot be verified because a check genuinely fails is honest; one that verifies because the failing check was moved somewhere nothing runs is not. DISCLOSURE ADDED 2026-07-29, to the entry's own standard: this check asserts the HREF half only. Nothing here asserts the template also lacks a tabindex or a bound listener, so 'not a control' in this id means 'carries no href'. The tabindex half is uncheckable for the same reason as everywhere else in this entry — attribute_matches tests one attribute's VALUE against a pattern and treats absence as failure, so 'absent, or present but non-negative' cannot be expressed; the listener half is inert_row_has_no_activation_handler's gap.

Tier 4 because the rows are cloned client-side and do not exist in the served HTML — a statement about THIS component's rendering, not a missing capability. DECLARED LIMITATION added 2026-07-29 after the checkability seat noted the name claims more than the type asserts: the contract promises the row 'carries a genuine href AND remains keyboard-reachable', and this check covers only the href half. Keyboard-reachability needs an assertion about tabindex's VALUE being absent-or-non-negative, which attribute_matches cannot express (it tests one attribute's value against a pattern, and 'absent is acceptable' is precisely the case it treats as failure). Named here rather than left implied by the id.

REASON CHANGED 2026-07-28. This used to be deferred because no attribute assertion existed at any tier. It now exists, and the reason is different and narrower: the inert rows are cloned client-side, so a static evaluation matches zero elements and correctly declines rather than passing vacuously (verified against the live page today). The executable form of the no-inert-control invariant for this component, waiting only on a browser.

checks._unsupported: NEW 2026-07-28, answering the council's [high] finding that a third of the must_not had no check at all, not even a deferred one. No event-listener assertion exists at EITHER tier — this is a distinct missing capability from attribute assertion, not another instance of it, and it is recorded separately so the harness backlog does not read as one gap when it is two. It is also the hardest half to see by eye: a row can carry no href and no tabindex and still be made clickable by a listener, which looks inert in the markup and behaves as a control.

checks.note: NEW 2026-07-29, and it exists because the council found reuse I had missed: deferral_honesty pointed out that the executable `interaction` type can click the inert row and assert the outcome, which is a real proxy for 'no activation handler' rather than another deferral. Taken. WHAT IT CATCHES: a click that NAVIGATES — the expected container would be gone from the new page, so the check fails. WHAT IT DOES NOT CATCH, stated because the id could be read as broader: an in-place state change. `expect` carries only selector and text_matches, so 'nothing happened' is not directly expressible, and a handler that opened something without navigating would pass this. It is a partial proxy, deliberately kept alongside inert_row_has_no_activation_handler rather than replacing it. Tier 4 because the inert rows are cloned client-side and no static evaluation can click anything.

REASON CORRECTED 2026-07-29, because the council was right and my earlier reason was not. I wrote that asset_loads 'matches the path as TEXT in the page HTML' as though that were an inherent property. It is not — it is the current implementation (check_tool_acceptance.go: strings.Contains(html, ch.Path)), and the seat correctly named it an implementation quirk rather than a proof that the type could not fetch the path and check its status. THE HONEST REASON IS DIFFERENT AND STRONGER: making asset_loads fetch would change what it MEANS for the 63 doc_plans criteria fences already using it, and under the owner's ruling of 2026-07-29 (RFC 002 §9 Q1) a change to what a shared mechanism guarantees is architecture-scope and needs its own RFC. So this clause is blocked on a governed change to a shared type, not on a missing capability — a materially different kind of blocked, and one this entry must not resolve unilaterally.

REQUIRES TIER 4. The rows are cloned client-side, so the served HTML carries only the template. At Tier 2 selector_count collapses to the container's anchor — exactly what list_exists already asserts — so this would pass while saying nothing about rows. DECLARED LIMITATION, added 2026-07-28 after the council noted a quantity-sounding name with no quantity: no checker reads a minimum or expected count (a `min` key would be an inert field, which the validator refuses), so even at Tier 4 this asserts THAT rows exist, never HOW MANY. It cannot distinguish a complete render from a partial one. Naming that here rather than letting the id imply otherwise.

checks._unsupported: NEW 2026-07-28, answering the council's 'this is a silent gap, not a declared limitation'. Nothing at either tier can INDUCE a feed failure and then assert the result: Tier 2 fetches one page as served, Tier 4 drives a real browser against the real feed, and neither can serve a broken one. Needs fault injection at the fetch boundary, which does not exist. Declared so the requirement survives with its reason attached rather than looking covered. MECHANISM, added 2026-07-29 for the same reason: serve the page with the feed path returning 404 (and separately, malformed JSON), then assert that the element matching list_container has no children beyond item_template and that empty_state_selector is still visible. The missing capability is the first clause — a fetch-boundary fault the runner can inject — not the assertion.

NEW 2026-07-28, answering the council's finding that absence_semantics — the clause the description leans on for its 'no invented participation numbers' honesty pitch — had no check and no deferral note. Asserting it needs a per-row conditional: for each rendered row, the stat slot is present iff that row's record carries a stat. No check type expresses a per-element condition tied to the source data, at either tier. This is a third distinct capability gap, recorded as its own. SPEC, added 2026-07-29 after the seat noted this was a placeholder rather than a runnable spec: for each rendered row, the element matching stat_slot_selector is present-and-visible IF AND ONLY IF that row's feed record carries the 'stat' field. The comparison is between the rendered DOM and the source record for the SAME row, which is why no existing type expresses it — every check we have takes a selector and looks at the page alone.

NEW 2026-07-29, answering the checkability seat: the empty_list state — 'the empty-state line remains visible; it is hidden only after at least one row renders' — was the one clause left with neither a check nor a deferral, which is the exact silence this entry spent a revision removing everywhere else. It needs two things we lack: an empty-region/visibility assertion (innerText on a display:none subtree falls back to textContent, so 'nothing is shown here' is not observable), and the ability to assert a relationship BETWEEN two states rather than one state at a time. Same missing capability as absent_optional_field_hides_its_slot.

NEW 2026-07-29, answering the checkability seat: data_contract.required_per_row names 'title' as required and nothing asserted it. No non-empty-text assertion exists at either tier — Tier 2's expect struct carries a selector and nothing else, and selector_exists on a rendered row says the element is there, not that it has content. This is a fourth distinct capability gap (text-content assertion), recorded as its own rather than folded into an existing one.

checks.note: RE-ENCODED 2026-07-29 after the council read the record this produced. Marked `_unsupported` it hit the validator's 'marked deferred although every part of it is executable today' branch — a deferral record with an empty field key and a self-contradicting message, which the deferral_honesty seat correctly called an unfinished placeholder. THE UNDERLYING GAP IS THE VALIDATOR'S, NOT THIS ENTRY'S: `selector_count` is an executable TYPE, but this INSTANCE asserts nothing because no checker reads a maximum, minimum or expected count, and the validator has no way to say 'the type runs but this instance would be vacuous'. That is the IMPLEMENTED-vs-SATISFIABLE distinction with no vocabulary for it. Encoded as tier 4 here, which is true (only a browser sees the rendered rows at all) and produces an honest record; the validator gap is recorded in NOTES 2026-07-29b for a separate change.

_REVISION_2026-07-29: Round 3. The council's gating [high] was that re-tiering template_row_not_a_control to 4 — when the Tier 2 check exists and FAILS — 'reads as evasion'. It was right, and it matched a suspicion I had already logged about my own reasoning, so the check is back at Tier 2 and the entry now carries a real failure rather than a hidden question. Four silent gaps the seats found (the empty_list clause, keyboard-reachability, required 'title', and two deferrals that were placeholders rather than specs) are each declared or specified. The one objection NOT answered is deferral_honesty [high] #2 — that the central rule is 100% unasserted on live rows — because it is TRUE and not fixable by editing: the rows are cloned client-side, so only a browser can see them, and nothing in the register drives one yet. Saying so is the honest answer; making the ratio look better would mean exactly the move the same seat just caught.
_REVISION_2026-07-29b: Round 4. Both [high] objections were the council finding things I had got wrong or missed, not disagreements. (1) My reason for deferring feed_loads described an implementation quirk as though it were an inherent limit; the true reason is that fixing it would change what asset_loads means for 63 live documents, which the owner's 2026-07-29 ruling makes RFC-scope. (2) The seat spotted that the executable `interaction` type can proxy the activation-handler clause by clicking the inert row — real reuse I had not considered — so that check now exists, bounded honestly to what it actually catches. THE ONE OBJECTION THAT WILL NOT GO AWAY BY EDITING is deferral_honesty's ratio finding, and it should stop being re-litigated each round: this component renders its rows CLIENT-SIDE, so every clause about a live row is Tier 4 by physics, and nothing in the register drives a browser yet. This entry cannot honestly reach a good executable/deferred ratio until bind+verify runs at Tier 4. That is a statement about the harness, not about the entry, and the next revision should not try to improve the ratio by moving clauses around.

The description spelled out 'stripped of the template's placeholder href and left out of the tab order' — the invariant's own wording in narrative form, in the one field the earlier revision did not sweep. Lower stakes than a must_not, and still the same drift.
